messages:
maria: Heads up — onboarding sample (edge worker) is blowing up for ESM/TS users. TS 5.x + NodeNext moduleResolution yields a ton of overload/generic errors around our SDK chat APIs. Repro is trivial in the sample app.

kevin: ugh, any error paste? steps to repro? :eyes:

maria: Steps: clone the starter, `pnpm i`, set RI_KEY, run `pnpm dev` (vite+edge). Import is the ESM entrypoint: 
```js
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference';
const c = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RI_KEY });
await c.chat.create({ model: 'r-instruct', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }] });
```
errors when compiling the edge bundle: 
```
TS2345: Argument of type '{ model: string; messages: { role: string; content: string; }[]; }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'ChatCreateParams<T>'...
Overload 1 expects 1 generic but got something that fails constraint 'T extends Record<string, unknown>'.
```

jen: hmm. does the sample tsconfig use `module: 'ESNext'` or `NodeNext`? Edge runtimes + bundlers are weird.

maria: sample uses NodeNext + moduleResolution: bundler to match Vite. Tried switching to ESNext and `skipLibCheck` temporarily — that silences the compiler but it's a bandaid.

sam: common pattern: our declaration file uses overloads that rely on `any` in some branches and `unknown` in others, TS picks the wrong candidate under NodeNext resolution. CJS consumers (require/main) were fine right?

maria: yup, CJS consumers are OK. Only ESM + edge bundler flows fail at dev time.

tyler: we ship: "main" -> cjs, "module" -> esm, and types -> dist/index.d.ts. Conditional exports include types variations. Bundlers sometimes pick the wrong .d.ts because of `exports`/typesVersions interplay. Could be a typesVersions or package.json exports bug.

kevin: can you paste the top of the generated .d.ts around chat.create? suspect the generic overloads are too permissive.

maria: pasted excerpt: 
```ts
export function createClient<T = any>(opts: ClientOpts): Client<T>;
export function createClient(opts: ClientOpts): Client<Record<string, any>>;
```
then chat.create has overloads like: 
```ts
chat.create<T extends ChatSchema = DefaultChatSchema>(params: ChatCreateParams<T>): Promise<ChatResult<T>>;
chat.create(params: ChatCreateParams<any>): Promise<ChatResult<any>>;
```
TS resolves the second but then later generic constraints mismatch.

jen: 2 quick mitigations: 1) avoid ambiguous overloads — keep a single generic signature with sensible defaults (use `unknown` for input types and `any` only where we must), 2) add a tiny `.d.ts` shim for the ESM entry that has explicit non-generic overloads used by the samples.

chris: I can take a stab. Plan: add a minimal typings patch to `src/types/esm-shim.d.ts` that re-exports safer overloads, then adjust build to emit it under the ESM export path. Also add a sample `tsconfig.json` in the starter that sets `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` or `node16` depending on bundler.

sam: also add `typesVersions` in package.json to point old TS compilers at the non-generic signatures, and modern ones at generic ones. But careful — typesVersions only works for npm resolution, not all bundlers.

maria: CI btw showed this failing on the sample starter in the last nightly run, here's the job: https://ci.company/ci/12345 — `ci-bot` flagged it.

ci-bot: Failure: sample-starter (edge) — TS build error in dev: 1 error. See log: https://ci.company/ci/12345/logs/edge-compile.txt

tyler: good catch. chris — if you open a draft PR, tag it w/ `devex` and `types` we'll get reviews. Also add a small repro repo link in the PR description showing the exact tsconfig + bundler that breaks.

chris: will do. probable changes: 
- collapse ambiguous overloads into a single generic with `unknown` defaults
- add an ESM shim types file for edge consumers
- update starter tsconfig and README notes about NodeNext vs bundler resolution
- add test that compiles the starter with TS 5.x NodeNext config

kevin: :+1: please include a short explanation of why `unknown` is safer than `any` for our generics in the PR. will help reviewers.

maria: thanks — after this we should also audit our other SDKs for similar overload fallthroughs (embeddings, tools).

jen: also log a ticket for the product docs team to add a blurb in onboarding about tsconfig + module resolution gotchas for edge runtimes.

sam: tiny nit — if we change defaults to `unknown`, make sure runtime converters (JSON->typed) still accept plain objects (use helper `as any as T` internally), otherwise consumers will hit runtime mismatch.

chris: noted. will add internal cast helpers and tests. opening draft PR in ~2h and will post link here.

maria: awesome — thanks everyone. we should unblock the new hires doing the bootcamp today. :party_parrot:
